policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 9 Apr close (1x4 3.85, 3x6 3.90, 6x9 3.99, 9x12 4.12 vs WIBOR 3M 3.85) price roughly 25bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 9 Apr; Glapiński sees no near-term change either way - hikes only in a 'black scenario' of renewed war, a question mark over cuts. Kotecki (2 Apr): the March cut was the last this year; Litwiniuk (2 Apr): no cuts soon, hikes possible if inflation worsens. March flash CPI 3.0% (31 Mar; 3.3% expected); core 2.5% in February. The fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise) takes ~0.9pp off April CPI (ING, PKO).
policy.risk_text: The ceasefire unwound much of the hike pricing; the risk is a breakdown of the truce (Hormuz still largely shut) re-pricing hikes, while the MPC's bar for a move either way is high. Long end: three April sales plus the USD issue, and a ~7% deficit.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026 (Inflation Report, 6 Mar); the NBP forecaster survey (1 Apr) has 2026 CPI at 2.9%. The next projection comes in July.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.2% of GDP (GUS preliminary, 1 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; S&P (2-6 Apr) sees a 2026 deficit of 7.0% of GDP (8.0% in an oil-shock case); budget deficit after February PLN 48.5bn; fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise, price caps) from 27-31 Mar.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~41% (end-Q1) financed; USD 6bn of 5Y/10Y/30Y priced on 7 Apr (UST +65/+105/+130bp); budget accounts PLN 169.5bn at end-March. No rating action in April; S&P reviews Poland on 8 May (A-, stable); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut to 3.75% on 4 Mar and held on 9 Apr; March CPI 3.0% y/y; 2025 GDP 3.6%, Q4 4.0%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 9 Apr: the MPC held at 3.75% as expected; the statement names commodity prices, fiscal policy and fuel-price regulation as CPI risks; Glapiński sees no near-term change either way - hikes only in a 'black scenario' of renewed war, a question mark over cuts; the NBP's 2025 loss was PLN 35.7bn; budget accounts PLN 169.5bn at end-March; yields rose slightly after the decision. Abroad: the truce wobbled as Iran capped Hormuz transits over Israeli strikes on Lebanon; Brent back to ~$97-99, Bund 10Y 2.99%; US February core PCE 3.0%; odds of a 2026 Fed cut fell to ~30% from 56%.

calendar.plan_text: MoF April plan (31 Mar): sale auctions on 15 Apr (PLN 4-12bn; OK0128, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1035, NZ0936), 23 Apr (6-14bn) and 28 Apr (5-13bn; new 10Y DS0436 replaces DS1035 from 23 Apr); no switch; a 50-week T-bill on 10 Apr (3-6bn). Q2 plan: 7-8 sales for PLN 50-90bn and 1-2 switches. 2026 needs ~41% financed at end-Q1. 7 Apr: USD 6bn issue (5Y 4.645%, 10Y 5.405%, 30Y 6.233%).
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it. April is back to regular supply: remaining sales 15 Apr, 23 Apr, 28 Apr. Next MPC 5-6 May: a hold is expected; the July projection is the next marker.

Poland's 5Y CDS was 60bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 257bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 9 Apr close). Truce wobbles; Brent back near $97 (9 Apr).
